title: Two physical regimes for the giant H II regions and giant molecular clouds in the Antennae galaxies
question: How do the physical properties of GMCs (ALMA CO(3-2)) and HII regions (GHaFaS Halpha) in the Antennae compare, and do they show two regimes (external pressure vs gravity dominated)?

data.bands: Band 7 CO(3-2) (Science Verification Band 7 per URL)

what.value: SMA CO(3-2) GMC catalogue of the Antennae, for comparison

evidence.quote: shows the mass-radius relation for molecular clouds (blue) compared with data of the Antennae from (cite: 2012ApJ...745...65U) (green)

what.value: M51 GMC properties incl. virial parameter

evidence.quote: We have added the GMCs detected in (cite: 2014ApJ...784....3C) for M51 since they estimated the virial parameter.
we were obliged to use the results of the GMC’s in the Milky Way from (cite: 2010ApJ...723..492R)

recipe.method: Primary-beam correct archival ALMA mosaics; build moment maps masked at 4 x rms

recipe.goal: Identify regions and measure size, sigma_v, flux
recipe.method: Dendrogram (bijection paradigm) on ALMA and GHaFaS cubes; second moments give R=1.91*sqrt(sig_maj sig_min)

recipe.goal: Derive GMC masses and virial parameters
recipe.method: CO luminosity (Solomon 1992) times alpha_CO, with factors 1.8 and 1.36; alpha_vir=5 sigma^2 R/(G M)
assumptions: D=22 Mpc, CO(1-0)/CO(3-2)=1.8, helium factor 1.36, spherical clouds

recipe.method: Dust-correct Halpha with HST Balmer decrement pixel by pixel; ionized mass M=1.57e-17 sqrt(L R^3); SFR via Kennicutt 2009; subtract natural (3 km/s) and thermal (9.1 km/s) widths
assumptions: Calzetti curve K(Ha)=3.33, K(Hb)=4.60; spherical uniform density; T=1e4 K

recipe.goal: Fit mass-radius relations and find regime break
recipe.method: Error-weighted linear fit for GMCs; double linear fit with free transition for HII regions
L_Ha-sigma_v envelope fit (minimum sigma per luminosity bin), shifted envelope criterion L>Lenv/40, virial parameter vs mass

evidence.quote: enabling us to identify 142 giant molecular clouds (GMCs) and 303 H regions
enabling us to identify 142 giant molecular clouds (GMCs) and 303 H regions
The transition at $\log(R_{\mathrm{HII}})=1.92$ corresponds to a transition at $\log(M_{\mathrm{HII}})=5.4$
We find a break in the molecular gas mass function at $\log(M_{\mathrm{mol}})\sim6.7$
the ionized gas to total gas fraction is $\sim 0.05$
